module_title: Banking and Financial Awareness: Digital Banking and NPCI Products (Level 2: Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate level focuses on the differences and limits of NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS, along with the functioning of UPI and FASTag. Questions regarding minimum/maximum transfer limits are guaranteed in IBPS PO and SBI PO exams.

core_concepts.title: NEFT vs RTGS vs IMPS
core_concepts.description:
1. NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer): Funds are settled in half-hourly batches (48 batches a day), not instantly. Available 24x7. No minimum or maximum limit.
2. RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement): Funds are settled continuously (Real-time) and individually (Gross). Used for high-value transactions. Minimum limit: ₹2 Lakhs. Maximum limit: None.
3. IMPS (Immediate Payment Service): Managed by NPCI. Provides instant 24x7 interbank electronic fund transfer. Maximum limit: ₹5 Lakhs per day.

core_concepts.title: UPI and BHIM
core_concepts.description: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) integrates multiple bank accounts into a single mobile application (like Google Pay, PhonePe). BHIM is the government's (NPCI's) own UPI app. The standard maximum transaction limit for normal UPI payments is ₹1 Lakh per day.

core_concepts.title: FASTag
core_concepts.description: An electronic toll collection system operated by NPCI under the NETC (National Electronic Toll Collection) program. It utilizes RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology for making toll payments directly from a linked prepaid or savings account.

important_entities.name: IFSC and MICR Codes
important_entities.key_fact: Essential codes for digital and physical fund transfers.
important_entities.significance: IFSC (Indian Financial System Code) is an 11-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies a bank branch (mandatory for NEFT/RTGS). MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) is a 9-digit numeric code used specifically for faster cheque clearance.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive trap in PO exams! Students assume NEFT has a minimum limit. Remember: You can send as little as ₹1 via NEFT and IMPS (No minimum limit). However, RTGS can ONLY be used if you are sending ₹2 Lakhs or more.

While the standard UPI limit is ₹1 Lakh, the RBI and NPCI have enhanced the limit to ₹5 Lakhs for specific categories like Capital Markets (IPOs), Retail Direct Scheme, hospital bills, and educational institution fees.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Since NEFT settles in half-hourly batches, a 24-hour day will have exactly 48 settlement batches (24 x 2). NEFT operates 24x7, 365 days a year.

exam_strategy_tips: For PO and Clerk Mains, specifically remember the technology behind FASTag (RFID) and the recently enhanced upper limit of IMPS (increased from ₹2 Lakhs to ₹5 Lakhs).
